table.title: January (First Month) 1938
table.caption_extra: Calendar for the Year January to December, 1938 (heading printed above the January table). Calendar for 1938 (anniversaries day by day). Column headings: Day of — Month, Week, Moon.

rows: New Year’s Day. Bank Holiday. Rendition of Mixed Court 1927. Likin abolished 1931. China’s fiscal year begins 1938.
Bank Holiday. Shanhaikwan occupied by Japanese 1933.
Customs and Bank Holiday. Hankow British Concession entered by Communist mob 1927.
Twelfth Night. Edict forbidding trade with Great Britain for ever 1840. Dr. V. K. Ting died 1936.
Shanghai Club’s new building opened 1911. First British Bishop of Church of China consecrated 1929. Small Cold.
Russian Christmas Day. Kiukiang British Concession looted 1927. Canton-Kowloon motor road opened 1938.
F. W. Maze appointed Inspector General of Customs 1929.
Plow Monday. Treaty of Versailles signed and League of Nations came into being 1920. Tsingtao occupied by Japanese 1938.
King’s Daughters’ Society founded, New York 1886. Hongkong seamen’s strike began 1922.
Russian New Year. Shanghai General Hospital returned to permanent quarters after evacuation 1938.
Thermometer 8 deg. Fah. at Shanghai 1893. Rendition of Tientsin Belgian Concession 1931. Hangchow-Nanchang Railway opened 1936.
Sir Alexander Hosie born 1853. Loss of C.M. str. Hsin Wah 1929.
Great opium burning at Shanghai 1919. New Masonic Temple, Shanghai, foundation stone laid 1931.
Asiatic Society of China (later China Branch of R.A.S.) founded, Hongkong 1847.
Japanese mob attacked S.M.P. Chinese constables 1932. King George V died 1936.
Hongkong taken possession of by British 1841. Loss of Chi. str. Heng Chong 1929. Great Cold.
Catholic diocese of Macao founded 1576. China-Italy direct radio service inaugurated 1935.
Dr. Albert Porges shot on Outside Road, Shanghai 1932. Gen. Han Fu-chu executed 1938.
Osaka “Asahi” founded 1879. First Italian Ambassador presented credentials, Nanking 1935. Kitchen God’s Ascension Day.
General Gordon born 1833. S.M.C. declared State of Emergency, S.V.C. mobilized, Japanese marines moved into Chapei, Shanghai 1932.
Death penalty decree against Christianity in China 1833. Chapei first bombed by Japanese seaplanes 1932. C.N. str. Tungchow pirated 1935.
President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s birthday (1882). National Government moved to Loyang 1932.
Bank Holiday. Birthday of Princess Beatrice of the Netherlands (1938). Whangpoo frozen over at Woosung 1886. Sir Francis Aglen dismissed by Chinese Government 1927. Spring Holiday.

table.title: February (Second Month) 1938
table.caption_extra: Calendar for 1938 (anniversaries day by day). Column headings: Day of — Month, Week, Moon.

rows: Bank Holiday. Emperor of Manchoukuo’s birthday (1906). Great Britain recognized Soviet 1924. Tariff Autonomy operative 1929. Spring Holiday.
Bank Holiday. Candlemas. Nanking shelled by Japanese 1932. Birthday of Heavenly Dragon. Spring Holiday.
Japanese bombarded Woosung forts 1932. Government radio station opened at Chenju 1934. Weihaiwei icebound (first time for nearly a century) 1936.
Col. C. A. Lindbergh’s birthday (1902). Philippine-American war began 1799. Beginning of Spring.
British flag hoisted at Singapore 1819. Nine Power Treaty signed, Washington 1922. Peking treasures removed to Shanghai 1933.
First official French Jesuits arrived in Peking 1688. First conference of National Medical Association of China 1916.
Russo-Japanese War began 1904. Provisional Court Agreement renewed 1933.
Second Japanese bombardment of Woosung Forts 1932.
Trans-Siberian mail service reopened 1935. Direct radio-telephonic communication Italy-China 1935. New subsidiary coinage issued 1936.
Japanese Constitution Day. Emperor of Manchoukuo’s birthday (1906). King of Egypt’s birthday (1920).
Hongkong and Shanghai Bank’s first general meeting 1866. Manchu abdication edicts published 1912.
St. Valentine’s Day. Singapore Naval Base opens 1938. Feast of Lanterns.
Penny postage began Shanghai-Britain by British P.O. 1902. Yuan Shih-kai elected President 1912. China-Japan commercial radio telephone 1936.
Lithuanian Independence Day. Insurgents evacuated Shanghai 1855.
Two British sailors killed by Chinese shells 1932. Lester School, Shanghai, foundation stone laid 1934.
Ex-Emperor Hsuan Tung Chief Executive of Manchoukuo 1932. Rain Water.
Sir Robert Hart born, Portadown 1835. Chen-O’Malley Agreement, Hankow 1927.
A. R. Margary murdered in Yunnan 1875.
George Washington born 1732. Death of Emperor Tao Kwang 1850. Death of Empress Dowager Lung Yu 1913.
Emperor Tung Chih enthroned 1873. Ex-Emperor Hsuan Tung arrived Tientsin 1925. Hungjao and Soochow aerodromes bombed by Japanese 1932.
Esthonian Independence Day. Japanese Delegation withdrew from League of Nations Assembly 1933.
H.R.H. Princess Alice’s birthday (Countess of Athlone) (1883).
Portuguese Coy, S.V.C., formed 1906. Hangchow aerodrome bombed by Japanese 1932. Military revolt in Tokyo 1936.
U.S. Legation to China opened, Macao 1844.
Game hunting ends. General strike in Hongkong 1922. Sino-Japanese delegates met on H.M.S. Kent 1932. New Shanghai Race Club buildings opened 1934.

table.title: March (Third Month) 1938
table.caption_extra: Calendar for 1938 (anniversaries day by day). Column headings: Day of — Month, Week, Moon.

rows: St. David’s Day. Chungking formally opened to trade 1891. State of Manchoukuo created 1932. Coronation of Emperor Kang Tê of Manchoukuo 1934.
Ash Wednesday. Chen-O’Malley Kiukiang Agreement 1927. Central Govt. assumed jurisdiction over Spanish nationals 1937.
Mohammedan New Year (1957). Japanese ceased hostilities, Shanghai 1932. Earthquake and tidal wave in Japan 1933.
First Sunday in Lent. Empress of Japan’s birthday (1903). Loss of C.N. str. Antung 1933. Birthday of Mencius. Excited Insects.
International Women’s Day. British str. Leechuen ascended Rapids 1898. Chang Hsueh-liang resigned 1933. Shanghai-Nanking air mail 1929.
H.B.M. Supreme Court for China established 1865. Germany declared war on Portugal 1916.
Japanese Army Day. Provisional Constitution of China adopted 1912. Tael abolished 1933.
China’s provisional constitution promulgated 1912. Hongkong University opened 1912. “New Life Movement” inaugurated at Nanchang 1934.
Customs Holiday. Russian revolution broke out 1917. Death of Sun Yat-sen 1925. Arbor Day.
China broke off relations with Germany 1917. Lytton Commission arrived in Shanghai 1932. U.S.S. Fulton on fire in Bias Bay 1933.
Emperor of Iran’s birthday (1878). Yunnan earthquake 1925. Nazi flag hoisted at German Consulate, Shanghai 1933.
Nanking captured by T’ai P’ing rebels 1852. British troops occupied Kowloon 1860.
Iranian New Year. Shanghai Day. King of Iraq’s birthday (1912). Shanghai City captured by Nationalists 1927. Spring Equinox.
Emperor K’ang Hsi issued edict of religious toleration 1692. Death of Sir Harry Parkes 1885. Haiho River Conservancy Board constituted 1901.
Chinkiang British Concession evacuated by foreigners 1927. C.E.R. transferred to Manchoukuo 1935.
Royal Asiatic Society’s Museum founded 1874. Nanking Outrages 1927. Sino-Japanese Peace Conference 1932. Hongkong-Penang air service 1936.
Macao formally ceded to Portugal 1887. Japan ceased to be member of League of Nations, midnight 1935. S.M.C. election declared invalid 1936.
Port Arthur and Dairen leased to Russia 1898.
Nanyang University founded 1896. Shanghai-Nanking Railway opened 1908.
Customs Holiday. C.N. str. Nanchang pirated 1933. Canton Martyrs’ Day.
New Land Regulations, Shanghai, approved 1881. Weihaiwei Regiment disbanded 1906.
Pope Pius XI’s birthday (1857). Duke of Gloucester’s birthday (1901). Chungking opened as treaty port 1890.

table.caption_extra: Calendar for 1938 (anniversaries day by day). Column headings: Day of — Month, Week, Moon.

rows: Electric trams started in Shanghai 1908. Shanghai District Court inaugurated 1930. Extension of Agreement regarding Chinese Courts in International Settlement for three years 1933.
British obtained lease of Weihaiwei 1898. Papal Holy Year began 1933.
Presentation of colours to Shanghai Russian Regiment 1932. Government control of Bank of China 1935. First mass wedding, Shanghai 1935.
Chusan evacuated by British 1846. Battle of Muddy Flat 1854. Mob attack on Hankow Japanese Concession 1927. Sino-Turkish Treaty of Amity 1934.
Spanish Republican Day. Wheelbarrow coolies’ strike, Shanghai 1897. Clear Brightness.
Decision to build church and parsonage, Shanghai 1847. U. S. A. entered Great War 1917. Raid on Soviet Embassy, Peking 1927.
Chinese advisory committee authorized by ratepayers 1920. Soviet embassy raided in Peking 1927. Chinwangtao occupied by Japanese 1933.
Soviet Consulate, Shanghai, searched by police, 1927. Birthday of Buddha.
Palm Sunday. Turnabout Light lit 1873. Chinese members elected to S.M.C. 1928. Shanghai-Canton Sikorsky plane lost with all on board 1934.
Gibraltar ceded to Britain 1713. Jung Lu, Grand Councillor to Empress Dowager, died 1903.
Decision to organize volunteer corps, Shanghai 1853. Dr. Nielsen, American medical missionary, kidnapped, Manchuria 1933.
Spanish Republican Day. First marriage in Holy Trinity Church, Shanghai 1852. St. John’s University corner stone laid 1879. Prof. W.E. Soothill died 1935.
Good Friday. Customs and Bank Holiday. Latvia’s Day. British Chamber of Commerce founded, Shanghai 1915. Nanking-Peking air mail 1931.
Easter Eve. Bank Holiday. British flag hoisted at Kowloon 1899. Manchoukuo oil monopoly law promulgated 1935.
Easter Sunday. Formosa, Pescadores and Liaotung ceded to Japan 1895. Chinese Boy Scouts Association inaugurated 1920.
Easter Monday. Bank Holiday. Great Northern Telegraph Co. opened, Shanghai 1871. Government removed from Peking to Nanking 1927.
Primrose Day. William Adams landed in Japan 1600. U.S.A. went off gold standard 1933.
Führer Adolf Hitler’s birthday (1889). Shengking, Kirin and Heilungkiang combined into Three Eastern Provinces 1907.
Princess Elizabeth’s birthday (1926). Formosan earthquake 1935. Corn Rain.
East India Company ceased to exist 1834. Lenin born 1870.
St. George’s Day. Sino-Netherlands and Sino-Norwegian extrality agreements signed 1931.
Sir Nicholas Hannen died, Shanghai 1900. Arms Embargo cancelled by Powers 1929.
Hana-mi (Japanese Cherry Blossom Festival). Ferdinand Magellan killed at Mactan, P.I., 1521.
Emperor of Japan’s birthday (1901). Hongkew Park bomb outrage 1932.
Princess Juliana of the Netherlands’ birthday (1909). Koxinga reached Taiwan 1661.

Anti-Christian riot, Yangchow 1891. Rome-Tokyo aviators arrived Shanghai 1920.
Polish National Day. Tsinanfu Incident 1928. “North-China Daily News” banned by Government 1929. Birthday of Genghiz Khan (1162).
Japanese Confucius Festival. Students’ “general” strike, Shanghai 1919.
Customs Holiday. Sun Yat-sen elected president 1921. Sino-Japanese peace agreement signed 1932. Draft Constitution promulgated 1936.
Shanghai University founded 1905. Lincheng Outrage 1923. Beginning of Summer.
Japan’s Ultimatum, 1915. First Iranian Consul arrived Shanghai 1934.
Christian community of Hangchow founded by Cattaneo 1611. Shanghai Settlement limits extended 1899. Two famine relief engineers kidnapped near Sianfu 1933.
Japanese Ultimatum accepted 1915. Italian Empire in Ethiopia inaugurated 1936. National Humiliation Day.
Joan of Arc’s Name Day. Ningpo City captured from Taipings 1862. Gordon captured Changchow 1864.
Matthew Ricci died, Peking 1610. Margaret Williamson Hospital founded, Shanghai 1885. Hu Han-min died 1936.
Anti-Christian riots in China 1891. Gen. J. W. N. Munthe died, Peiping 1935. Coronation of King George VI 1937.
Shanghai French Municipal Council inaugurated 1862. Chang Tso-lin declared independence 1922.
Old May Day. Mr. Henry Lester died, Shanghai 1926.
M. M. str. Georges Phillipar burnt in Indian Ocean 1932.
Norwegian National Day. China-Japan Legations elevated to Embassies 1935.
All Saints Church, Tientsin, destroyed by fire, 1935.
Cuban National Day. Allies took Peiho Forts 1858. Lindbergh flew Atlantic 1927.
C. P. O. strike, Shanghai 1932. Bells of Holy Trinity Cathedral dedicated 1932. Asiatic Petroleum Co. withdraws from Manchoukuo 1936.
Trinity Sunday. Boxer Rising began 1900. Kansu Earthquake 1927.
Empire Day. Union Insurance Society of Canton, Ltd., formed 1835. Holy Trinity Church foundation stone laid 1866. Volcanic eruption in Hokkaido 1926.
Ascension Day. Queen Mary’s birthday (1867). Tientsin British Concession ceded 1858.
Japanese Navy Day. Hoshun Maru pirated near Tangku 1933.
Treaty of Aigun (Russia-China) 1858. First meeting of Hongkong Chamber of Commerce 1861.
U. S. A. Decoration Day. Nanking Road Incident, Shanghai 1925. Death of Fleet-Admiral Marquis Togo 1934.
South African Union Day. China recognized Soviet 1924. Last of Japanese expeditionary force left Shanghai 1932. Sino-Japanese truce signed at Tangku 1933.

table.caption_extra: Calendar for 1938 (anniversaries day by day). Column headings: Day of — Month, Week, Moon.

Customs and Bank Holiday. Opening of Country Club, Shanghai 1879. Censorate and Hanlin Academy abolished 1912. Dragon Boat Festival.
Italian Constitution Day. Lin Tseh-hsu’s opium burning, Canton 1839. J. Hudson Taylor, founder C.I.M., died, Changsha 1905.
Sir Thomas Jackson born 1841. Chang Tso-lin killed in train wreck 1928.
Whit Sunday. Communication with Peking cut 1900.
Whit Monday. Death of Yuan Shih-kai 1916. Sprouting Seeds.
Kuomintang flag hoisted in Peking 1928. J. H. Thorburn killed by military in Soochow 1931.
Official observance of King George VI’s birthday. Franco-Chinese peace treaty signed, Tientsin 1885. Loss of H.M.S. Poseidon 1931.
Luis de Camoëns died 1580. Margary memorial unveiled, Shanghai 1885.
Trinity Sunday. East India Co.’s ship Clove arrived Japan 1613. First railway in Japan opened 1872.
Anti-foreign riot at Kiukiang 1925. State of Emergency officially ended, Shanghai 1932.
Chinese Company, S.V.C., formed 1906. First Japanese Ambassador presented credentials 1935.
Dr. J. H. Ingram shot by robbers near Peiping 1934. First British Ambassador presented credentials 1935.

Shanghai taken 1842. Bomb attack on Governor of Indo-China, Canton 1924. Shameen strike began 1925.
Extermination of foreigners ordered 1900; Baron von Kettler murdered, Peking 1900. French Tramways strike began, Shanghai 1930.
Dr. Griffith John arrived in Hankow 1861. Tientsin massacre 1870. Summer Solstice
Duke of Windsor’s birthday (1894). Robert Hart appointed British Minister 1885. Attack on Shameen 1925. Creation of Heaven and Earth.
Midsummer Day. Port of Hulutao declared open 1930.
Capt. John Weddell’s squadron reached Macao 1638.
Sir Henry Pottinger, first Governor of Hongkong, appointed 1843. Tientsin peace treaty signed 1858.
Treaty between France and China signed 1858.

Emperor of China gave first audience to foreign Ministers 1873. Shanghai Waterworks opened 1883. Peiping-Hongkong one-day plane service 1937.
Mr. (afterwards Sir Robert) Hart appointed Officiating Inspector General of Customs 1861. Section of Woosung Railway opened 1876. United States Court for China established 1906.

table.title: July (Seventh Month) 1938
table.caption_extra: Calendar for 1938 (anniversaries day by day). Column headings: Day of — Month, Week, Moon.

rows: Dominion Day (Canada). Bank Holiday. “North-China Daily News” established 1864. Kailan Mining Administration’s Silver Jubilee 1937. Summer Holiday.

Wanghsia Treaty (U.S.A.-China) 1844. H.M. Supreme Court established Shanghai 1865. Chiang Kai-shek entered Peking 1928.
King George V and Queen Mary married 1893.
Emperor Hsuan Tung abdicated 1917. City Government of Greater Shanghai inaugurated 1927. Lukouchiao Incident 1937.

First Municipal Council elected, Shanghai 1854. Temperature in Tientsin reached 110° Fah. 1934.

Chao Ti-chao, gen. manager C.M.S.N. Co., assassinated 1930.
Papal Envoy arrived at Mongol Court 1246.
Chinese Post Office in Manchuria closed 1932. Feast of Heavenly Gifts.
Emperor Haile Selassie’s birthday (1891). Manchurian Post Offices seized by Manchoukuo 1932. Great Heat.

Chapei temporarily occupied by Shanghai Municipal Council 1913.
Peruvian National Day. Shells burst in Public Gardens, Shanghai 1913. Sino-Japanese hostilities open 1937. Japanese massacred, Tungchow 1937.
Signor Mussolini’s birthday (1883). Tientsin bombarded by Chinese and Japanese 1937.
French Mixed Court handed over to China 1931. First National State Lottery drawn 1933.
Foreign vessels allowed temporarily to engage in Japanese coastal trade 1937.
